summary: Case-006 (b.cetin@aegean.edu): Escalate, confidence 0.6. Single verified signal F1 [LIKELY 0.6]: first-time sign-in from unseen device PH-9900 for account normally using LT-6002 (ATT&CK T1078). Password-spray claims from 78.187.4.44 and 193.140.10.17 were rejected; both IPs belong to shared-NAT ASN Turkcell with 72/72 and 61/61 failures respectively, consistent with background noise. Risk Gate escalates per evidence policy despite degraded model step proposing monitor.

risk.rationale: The only verified finding is F1: a sign-in from a previously unseen device PH-9900 (usual device LT-6002), LIKELY 0.6, mapped to T1078. The two password-spray-then-success claims from 78.187.4.44 and 193.140.10.17 were rejected with valid critics—both IPs belong to shared-NAT ASN Turkcell, and the high failure counts across many accounts are consistent with background noise rather than a coordinated spray. With no confirmed account takeover chain and the stronger intrusion claims explained away, the remaining new-device sign-in is a weak unexplained signal appropriate for monitoring rather than containment or escalation.
